title: File read/write broken: server shotguns {filePath,file_path,path} ignoring tool schema (claude/qwen reject it), and Write targets the plan file not the user's file (v0.297.1)
body:
## Summary

File **read and write** through agentic CLIs are broken on **v0.297.1** due to the server emitting hardcoded, shotgunned parameter names that ignore the advertised tool schema, plus a write flow that targets the internal plan file instead of the user's file. Seen in the Claude Code TUI and reproduced at the API. Please add dedicated read/write regression tests across all CLIs.

## Bug 1 — Read: server shotguns `{filePath, file_path, path}`, ignoring the tool schema

The server always emits **all three key variants at once**, regardless of what the tool declares:

```
advertise Read (required ["file_path"], additionalProperties:false)  -> {"filePath":"1.txt","file_path":"1.txt","path":"1.txt"}
advertise read_file (required ["path"])                              -> {"filePath":"1.txt","file_path":"1.txt","path":"1.txt"}
advertise read_file (required ["absolute_path"])                     -> {"filePath":"1.txt","file_path":"1.txt","path":"1.txt"}
```

Consequences:
- **Claude Read** has `additionalProperties:false` and rejects the extras — exactly the TUI error:
  ```
  <tool_use_error>InputValidationError: Read failed due to the following issues:
  An unexpected parameter `filePath` was provided
  An unexpected parameter `path` was provided</tool_use_error>
  ```
- **qwen read_file** requires `absolute_path`, which isn't in the blob at all → read fails entirely.

Same root cause as #744 / #749 / #750-comment: hardcoded parameter names instead of honoring each harness's advertised schema. The server must emit **only** the key(s) the advertised tool declares.

## Bug 2 — Write: targets the internal plan file, and fails

`write 10 to 1.txt file` emits a `Write` whose `content` is a **`general_change_plan` .lino document** and whose path is **`.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino`** — not the user's content ("10") to `1.txt`:

```
Write args: {
  "content": "general_change_plan\n  id \"...\"\n  goal \"write 10 to 1.txt file\"\n  target \"1.txt\"\n  step 1 ... \n",
  "filePath": ".formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino",
  "file_path": ".formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino",
  "path": ".formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino"
}
```

In the Claude TUI this surfaces as **`Error writing file` (twice)** and the user's `1.txt` is not updated with "10". The plan-first design is fine internally, but the user-visible Write must ultimately write the requested content ("10") to the requested file (`1.txt`), and use the tool's declared parameter names so it doesn't error.

## Bug 3 — `execute ls` / read non-determinism

Across turns in the same session, `execute ls` sometimes returns the real listing (`1.txt`) and sometimes `I could not determine (no content) ... unknown`. Read/list should be deterministic.

## Expected

1. Emit **only** the advertised tool's declared parameter name(s) for Read/Write/Edit/list tools (claude `file_path`; qwen `absolute_path`/`path`; codex/others as advertised). No shotgunning; no `additionalProperties` violations.
2. Write must persist the **user's content to the user's target file**; the plan file is internal and must not be the user-visible Write target or block the real write.
3. Make read/list deterministic.
4. **Add read/write regression tests** exercising: create → read back → write/overwrite → read back → append → delete, in a temp dir, across codex, agent, gemini, qwen, opencode, grok, cursor (claude excluded from the sweep), in all supported natural languages.

## Repro
```
formal-ai serve --port 8080 --agent-mode &
curl -s localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"model":"formal-ai","tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"Read","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"file_path":{"type":"string"}},"required":["file_path"],"additionalProperties":false}}}],"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"read 1.txt"}]}' \
 | jq -r '.choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function.arguments'
# => {"filePath":"1.txt","file_path":"1.txt","path":"1.txt"}   (claude rejects filePath/path)
```

## Environment
formal-ai 0.297.1 (`cargo install formal-ai`), macOS arm64, Claude Code v2.1.212 (evidence only; not part of the automated sweep).

---

## Scope widening: read/write intent generalization + NL variations (v0.297.1)

Beyond the schema/shotgun bug above, read/write **intent recognition** is phrasing-gated and misroutes to unrelated tools (per #745 generalization mandate).

**read_file — 9/15; read intent leaks to web/exec:**
```
OK  read / read the file / show me the contents of / open / print / show / get the contents of / read file / show file  1.txt
XX  cat 1.txt              -> exec_command
XX  display 1.txt          -> web_fetch    (!)
XX  view the file 1.txt    -> web_search    (!)
XX  load 1.txt             -> web_fetch    (!)
XX  what is in 1.txt       -> UNKNOWN
XX  tell me what 1.txt contains -> UNKNOWN
```

**write_file — 7/15:**
```
OK  write X to / save X to / make a file …containing / write the text …into / create …with content hello / save the following to / append …to
XX  create a file 1.txt with hello   -> UNKNOWN
XX  put hello in 1.txt               -> UNKNOWN
XX  set the contents of 1.txt to hello -> read_file  (!)
XX  store / output / echo hello into 1.txt -> UNKNOWN / TEXT
XX  create file 1.txt / new file 1.txt with hello -> UNKNOWN
```

**Expected:** 10-20+ NL variations per language for read and for write must each resolve to the correct tool by generalization; a local filename must never route to web_fetch/web_search; write must persist the user's content to the user's file (not the plan file). Add a full read/write **lifecycle** regression across all CLIs and languages: create → read back → overwrite → read back → append → read back → edit/replace → read back → delete → confirm gone. Also test binary/large files, missing-file reads (natural "there is no such file" message per #750), and paths with spaces/unicode.

## Corroboration via real claude `-p` (isolated temp config, local server)

Running the official Claude CLI in `-p` mode against the local server (config redirected to a temp dir — never global):
```
formal-ai with --non-interactive --no-start-server claude "create a file hello.txt containing the text world"
# => server returns only a general_change_plan .lino (steps 1-3); hello.txt is NOT created on disk.
```
So the write flow is broken **end-to-end through a real harness**, not just at the API: it composes a plan (`.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino`) but never performs the actual file write. Confirmed `hello.txt` absent afterward.


---
## Implementation spec
- Use the argument-builder from #758 §B: emit **only** the advertised tool's declared key(s). For claude `Read`(`file_path`), qwen `read_file`(`absolute_path`), opencode `read`(`filePath`) — emit exactly that one key, nothing else.
- **Write must be two internal steps but one user-visible effect:** step 1 may append the plan to `.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino` (internal, not the user-visible Write), step 2 MUST emit a Write of the **user's content** to the **user's target path** (`1.txt` ← "10"), step 3 verify. The user-visible Write tool call's `content` = the requested content, `path` = the requested file — never the plan file.
- **Fixture (must pass) via real claude `-p`:** `create hello.txt containing world` → `hello.txt` exists on disk with `world`; the general_change_plan is internal only.
